known_anti_patterns: the fix is not replayed outside this session, so it is capped at PARTIAL_ALIVE under the promotion law regardless of the suite being green

this closes the Bash-write half of Checkpoint 3's first required-proof clause (edit refusal); the second clause -- refuse manufacture outside `actuation=manufacturing` -- remains entirely prompt-level and is untouched by this receipt

the fence keys off `agent_type`, a field this session confirmed present on real PreToolUse payloads for --agent-launched sessions; it has not been independently confirmed for every invocation shape Claude Code supports (e.g. Task-tool-spawned subagents were not separately probed against this exact fence)

a prior same-day pass tried to establish this same property by asking agents to self-report their own tool list; that method was independently shown unreliable (contradictory answers to an identical prompt across repeated runs) and is not relied on here -- this receipt's evidence is file-system fact (a file exists or does not) and an automated regression test, not model self-report

negative_falsifier.why_this_counts: parametrized on 'echo hi > /tmp/f.txt', 'echo hi >> /tmp/f.txt', 'cmd 2> err.log' -- these are exactly the bare-redirect shapes that were NOT classified as mutations before this cycle (only tee/cat-with-redirect were). Reverting the _BARE_REDIRECT addition in bash_classify.py makes this fail, which is the literal defect this receipt closes: a non-editor agent could write a file through Bash undetected by the classifier the whole control plane depends on.

positive_witness.why_this_counts: parametrized over all 7 non-manufacturing agents (cmca-allocator, config-law-architect, ecosystem-controller, ferroplan-planner, independent-validator, rdf-observer, receipt-auditor), invoking scripts/bash-write-fence.py as a real subprocess with a PreToolUse payload carrying each agent's real agent_type and asserting both a PermissionDecision deny and that the target file does not exist afterward. This is the mechanical enforcement Checkpoint 3 asks for, not a self-reported tool list: a live nested claude --plugin-dir session confirmed the same result for 2 of these 7 agents before this test existed, and this test now covers all 7 automatically and repeatably.

title: Bash-write fence for non-manufacturing agents
